nodes.name: Pt impregnation-reduction at 200°C
nodes.procedure: The subnano Pt clusters anchored on SnO2@NPC (Pt/SnO2@NPC-200) were obtained by impregnation method, following reduction in H2 atmosphere at 200°C to tune the Pt-SnO2 contact distance.
nodes.source_text: In order to tune the contact distance between Pt and SnO2... we further improve the thermal-treatment temperature during the subnano Pt clusters formation process as shown in Fig. 1a... Pt/SnO2@NPC-200

nodes.name: Pt impregnation-reduction at 300°C
nodes.procedure: The subnano Pt clusters anchored on SnO2@NPC (Pt/SnO2@NPC-300) were obtained by impregnation method, following reduction in H2 atmosphere at 300°C to generate more Pt-SnO2 interface and stronger interactions.
nodes.source_text: treatment temperature at 300°C induce the formation of stronger SMSI on the Pt/SnO2@NPC compared with other samples... Pt/SnO2@NPC-300

nodes.description: HER performance in N2-saturated 0.5 M H2SO4
nodes.source_text: All the electrochemical behaviors of all catalysts were used as a three-electrode system with acidic electrolytes... in N2 saturated 0.5M H2SO4 solution... Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 exhibited the highest HER catalytic activity with overpotential of only 11.7mV at 10mA·cm-2 among the Pt/SnO2@NPC, outperforming Pt/C catalyst (28@10mA cm-2)... The mass activity of the Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 at overpotential of 20mV is 4.08Amgpt-1... Tafel slope for Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 is only 23.3mVdec-1... highest TOF value of 4.13s-1 was found on Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 at 20mV... Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 maintained about 95% of the initial current after even 15h at a constant overpotential of 10mV. In addition, after 5000 cyclic voltammetry testing... the Pt loading is 4.43%

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Pt/SnO2@NPC show broad weak Pt diffraction peaks and weaker SnO2 peaks at 2θ = 26.61°, 33.89°, 51.78° compared to SnO2@NPC, confirming small Pt nanoclusters and confinement of SnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurement in Fig. 1b shown that, compared with NPC, the XRD pattern of SnO2@NPC presents three broad diffraction peaks at 2θ = 26.61°, 33.89°, 51.78°, confirming that we have successfully confined the very small sized SnO2 into NPC micropores.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images of Pt/SnO2@NPC show sub-nano Pt clusters with no evident lattice fringes, confirming sub-nano size; few bigger particles observed on Pt/SnO2@NPC-400 indicating sintering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The sub-nanoclusters can be detected on HRTEM images of all Pt/SnO2@NPC as shown in Fig. 1c, Fig. S3a and S5a, and there is no evident lattice fringes are noted, which demonstrates that the sub-nano Pt clusters achieved on SnO2@NPC.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images confirm sub-nanoclusters evenly dispersed on Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 with size distribution shown in inset.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM images as shown in Fig. 1d and Fig. S3-S5 also verified that the sub-nanoclusters evenly dispersed on the NPC for all Pt/SnO2@NPC catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Pt and SnO2 on Pt/SnO2@NPC-300.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The uniform Pt on Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 was further verified by the elemental mapping testing (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f XPS shows negative shift to lower binding energy in Pt/SnO2@NPC compared to Pt/NPC, largest shift at 300°C (72.21/75.50 eV for Pt(0), 73.11/76.40 eV for Pt(II)), indicating strongest SMSI and electron transfer from SnO2 to Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt 4f in Pt/SnO2@NPC at all temperatures shifted to the lower binding energy in comparison with Pt/NPC catalyst, arising from the enriched electron density of Pt due to electron transformation from the O element in SnO2 to Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: Sn 3d XPS shows peaks at 487.14/495.58 eV and 486.05/494.49 eV for Sn(IV) and Sn(0), with largest negative shift in Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 confirming stronger SMSI.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The largest negative shift of Sn 3d spectra on Pt/SnO2@NPC-300 confirms that the formation of more SMSI on the Pt/SnO2@NPC at 300°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS shows positive shift to higher energy in Pt/SnO2@NPC compared to SnO2@NPC, largest at 300°C with highest O2 content (48.78%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compare with SnO2@NPC, Pt/SnO2@NPC at all temperatures are shift to higher energy (Table S3). This suggests that the SMSI effect due to the binding of metal oxide and Pt change the electronic structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP testing shows Pt loading of 4.5 wt% in Pt/SnO2@NPC and 4.43 wt% after durability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt loading for Pt/SnO2@NPC is estimated to be 4.5% by ICP testing.
